For each of the 40 charts: the table it needs, column by column, and how each row becomes a mark; the data drawing it now, to copy as CSV or hand to another model; what it is best and worst for; and every other chart the same data makes, with an assessment of whether the switch helps, and for what.

area

A line with a soft filled area down to zero, for a trend where the amount itself matters.

Trend over time How each group or period splits Comparing amounts across categories

Best for

  • Volumes over time where the amount itself matters: cash, revenue, traffic
  • A forecast with its uncertainty band
  • How a stacked total splits over time (two to four series)

Least useful for

  • Several series that cross: the fills hide each other (use line)
  • Categories with no order (use bar)
  • Values that go below zero

The table it needs

One row is: One row per point in time, in order. How it is built: One point per row at x (in date order) and y; the area under the line is filled down to zero. Several y fields stack or overlap; a forecast field continues the line dashed, and a band (low, high) shades a range. Reads well with 4 to 400 rows.

OptionHoldsRequiredWhat it does
xdateyesField for the ordered axis, usually a date or period.
ynumber (one or more)yesField or fields for the values. Each field is one series.
forecastcategoryField that is true on forecast rows. From the last actual on, lines draw dashed in a softly shaded zone labelled Forecast, and the tooltip marks those rows. On an area the forecast's wash is fainter too. Unstacked areas only.

  • bullet: needs a separate column for target (it would reuse "cash", already the value)
  • bump: It needs one value per series in each period, to rank.
  • candlestick: needs a separate column for high (it would reuse "cash", already the open)
  • chord: It needs flows that go both ways between the same groups.
  • dumbbell: needs a separate column for to (it would reuse "cash", already the from)
  • funnel: It needs ordered stages that narrow, such as visits to sign-ups to sales.
  • likert: It needs answer counts on one ordered scale, such as disagree to agree.
  • meter: needs a separate column for target (it would reuse "cash", already the value)
  • rings: needs a separate column for target (it would reuse "cash", already the value)
  • sankey: It needs flows from a source to a target.
  • scatter: needs a separate column for y (it would reuse "cash", already the x)
  • slope: needs a separate column for to (it would reuse "cash", already the from)
  • timeline: It needs tasks with a start date.
  • variance: needs a separate column for target (it would reuse "cash", already the value)
  • waterfall: It needs changes that add up from one total to another.

bar

Vertical bars comparing amounts across categories.

Comparing amounts across categories Ranking, top to bottom Trend over time How each group or period splits Share of one whole Actual against target or plan Exact values and lookup

Best for

  • An amount across a handful of categories: revenue by region, orders by month
  • Two or three series side by side or stacked: Core and Plus by region
  • Monthly totals against a budget line

Least useful for

  • Long category names (use hbar)
  • More than about 15 categories (use hbar or treemap)
  • A long continuous trend (use line)

The table it needs

One row is: One row per category, each named once. How it is built: One bar per row at x, as tall as y. Several y fields make grouped bars, or stacked ones with stacked (percent for shares); a lines field draws a line such as a target across the bars. Reads well with 2 to 16 rows.

OptionHoldsRequiredWhat it does
xcategoryyesField for the categories along the horizontal axis.
ynumber (one or more)yesField or fields for bar heights. Each field is one series.
linesnumber (one or more)Field or fields drawn as lines over the bars, on the same axis, for example a target. Never a second axis. Under one target line (a field named target, plan, goal, budget or quota), bars on the wrong side of it (see goodWhen) are drawn outlined and keyed Below target.

beeswarm

A distribution: one dot per row along a value axis, nudged apart so none overlap, optionally one row per group.

How values spread Comparing amounts across categories Exact values and lookup

Best for

  • Every individual deal, order or response visible, with outliers you can name
  • Spread across a few groups in samples of tens to hundreds

Least useful for

  • Thousands of rows (use histogram)
  • Totals or shares (use bar or donut)

The table it needs

One row is: One row per thing measured (a deal, a ticket, a response); the chart counts or spreads them. How it is built: One dot per row along the value axis, nudged apart so none overlap; a group field gives each group its own row, and a label field names each dot on hover. Reads well with 10 to 400 rows.

OptionHoldsRequiredWhat it does
valuenumberyesNumeric field along the axis.
groupcategoryField giving each group its own labelled row.
labelcategoryField naming each dot in its tooltip.

boxplot

A box plot per group on one shared axis: a box over the middle half of the values (first to third quartile), a line at the median, whiskers to the furthest values within 1.5 box-widths, and dots for outliers beyond.

How values spread Comparing amounts across categories

Best for

  • Comparing medians and spread across groups: deal size by region, handle time by team
  • Spotting outliers in analytic reviews

Least useful for

  • Audiences who do not read quartiles (use beeswarm or ridgeline)
  • Fewer than about five values per group
  • Totals

The table it needs

One row is: One row per thing measured (a deal, a ticket, a response); the chart counts or spreads them. How it is built: Rows are grouped by group; each group's values give a box from the first to the third quartile, a line at the median, whiskers and outlier dots. Reads well with 15 to any number of rows.

OptionHoldsRequiredWhat it does
valuenumberyesNumeric field whose spread is drawn.
groupcategoryField giving each group its own box. Without it, all rows make one box.

bump

Rank over time: in every period the series are ranked by value (highest first), and each series is one smooth line through its ranks, named at both ends.

Ranking, top to bottom Trend over time

Best for

  • Who overtook whom

Least useful for

  • More than about ten series, or only one period

The table it needs

One row is: One row per combination of two categories, such as month and product. How it is built: Rows are one per period and series; in each period the series are ranked by value and each series is a line through its ranks. Reads well with 6 to any number of rows.

OptionHoldsRequiredWhat it does
xdateyesField with the period, such as a month. Periods keep the order of the rows.
seriescategoryyesField naming the series being ranked, such as a product.
valuenumberyesField the ranking is by; the highest value ranks 1.

donut

Part-to-whole at a glance: a ring of up to 6 slices with the total in the middle and a legend of values and shares.

Share of one whole A headline number Comparing amounts across categories

Best for

  • Share of one whole with two to five parts: revenue by segment, budget by team
  • An executive summary where the total matters too

Least useful for

  • More than six parts or close values (use hbar)
  • Comparing several wholes (use bar stacked to percent)
  • Change over time (use area)

The table it needs

One row is: One row per category, each named once. How it is built: One slice per row, its angle its share of the sum of value, with the total in the middle. Reads well with 2 to 6 rows.

OptionHoldsRequiredWhat it does
labelcategoryyesField naming each slice.
valuenumberyesField with each slice's amount. Zero, negative and missing values are left out.

fromnumberyesField with the before value.

gauge

One headline number on a half-circle scale: an arc filled from min to the value, a tick at the target, the number large inside the arc and the scale's ends below; with a target, a line under the arc says where it stands (Target met, or how far to go).

A headline number Actual against target or plan

Best for

  • One KPI against a goal on a known scale: NPS, utilization, SLA attainment

Least useful for

  • Several values (use bullet or meter)
  • Trends (use kpi with series)
  • Small differences, which the arc hides

The table it needs

One row is: One value; with more rows, the last one is the headline and the rest draw its trend. How it is built: The first row's value fills a half-circle from min to max, with a tick at target and the number in the middle. Reads well with 1 to 1 rows.

OptionHoldsRequiredWhat it does
valuenumberyesField holding the number.
targetnumberField holding the target, marked with a tick.

histogram

A distribution as touching bars: the value's range is cut into bins on round edges, and each bar counts the rows in its bin.

How values spread

Best for

  • The shape of one measure: deal sizes, response times, order values
  • Skew, clusters and the typical range

Least useful for

  • Comparing groups (use boxplot or ridgeline)
  • Fewer than about 20 values (use beeswarm)
  • Totals

The table it needs

One row is: One row per thing measured (a deal, a ticket, a response); the chart counts or spreads them. How it is built: The range of value is cut into bins on round edges; each bar counts the rows in its bin. Reads well with 20 to any number of rows.

OptionHoldsRequiredWhat it does
valuenumberyesNumeric field to bin.

horizon

Many time series at once, each in a thin row: values are measured from a baseline and folded into bands of deepening color, blue above and red below, so a dozen series fit where one line chart would.

Trend over time Comparing amounts across categories Actual against target or plan

Best for

  • Many series over time in little space: six to twenty regions, servers or stores
  • Deviation from plan, day by day, in operations monitoring

Least useful for

  • General audiences and exact values (use line)
  • One or two series

The table it needs

One row is: One row per point in time, in order. How it is built: One thin row per y field; each value is measured from a baseline and folded into bands of deepening color, blue above and red below. Reads well with 10 to any number of rows.

OptionHoldsRequiredWhat it does
xdateyesField for the ordered axis, usually a date.
ynumber (one or more)yesField or fields, one row each, such as a region's revenue against plan.

icicle

A hierarchy laid flat: a column for the total, then one per level left to right, each child splitting its parent's height by value, in lighter tints of its family's color.

Nested breakdowns Share of one whole Ranking, top to bottom

Best for

  • Deep breakdowns with long names: budget by unit, team and line
  • Drill paths, left to right

Least useful for

  • Flat data with one level (use hbar)
  • Negative values

The table it needs

One row is: One row per leaf of the hierarchy, its levels in columns from the top down. How it is built: A column for the total, then one per level; each child splits its parent's height by the sum of value. Reads well with 4 to 200 rows.

OptionHoldsRequiredWhat it does
levelscategory (one or more)yesFields from the top level down, one column each, for example ["region", "product", "plan"]. Up to 4.
valuenumberyesField sizing the cells. Zero and negative values are left out.

likert

Survey answers as diverging stacked bars: one bar per question, its responses in order from one pole to the other, centered on the neutral middle so disagreement grows left and agreement right.

Survey and rating answers Share of one whole Comparing amounts across categories

Best for

  • Comparing sentiment across questions

Least useful for

The table it needs

One row is: One row per category, each named once. How it is built: One bar per row (a question); its response fields, in order from one pole to the other, stack centered on the neutral middle. Reads well with 1 to 20 rows.

OptionHoldsRequiredWhat it does
labelcategoryyesField with each question.
responsesnumber (one or more)yesCount fields for the responses, in order from the negative pole to the positive, for example ["strongly_disagree", "disagree", "neutral", "agree", "strongly_agree"]. An odd count puts the middle one at the center.

line

Lines showing change over an ordered axis, usually time.

Trend over time Comparing amounts across categories Actual against target or plan

Best for

The table it needs

One row is: One row per point in time, in order. How it is built: One point per row at x (in order) and y, joined; each y field is one series, and reference lines mark targets. Reads well with 3 to 1000 rows.

OptionHoldsRequiredWhat it does
xdateyesField for the ordered axis, usually a date or period.
ynumber (one or more)yesField or fields for line values. Each field is one series.
forecastcategoryField that is true on forecast rows. From the last actual on, lines draw dashed in a softly shaded zone labelled Forecast, and the tooltip marks those rows.

marimekko

A mosaic: one column per category, as wide as its total, split into segments by each series' share of that column.

How each group or period splits Share of one whole Comparing amounts across categories

Best for

  • Market maps: how big each segment is and how it splits (region by product)
  • Sizing opportunities in strategy reviews

Least useful for

  • Many small segments
  • Precise values (use table)
  • Audiences new to mosaics (use bar stacked)

The table it needs

One row is: One row per combination of two categories, such as month and product. How it is built: One column per x category, as wide as its total; each column is split by series into segments as tall as their share. Reads well with 4 to 60 rows.

OptionHoldsRequiredWhat it does
xcategoryyesField naming each column, such as a region. Columns keep the order of the rows.
seriescategoryyesField naming the segments inside each column, such as a product.
valuenumberyesNumeric field sizing the segments; a column's width is the sum of its values.

pareto

The 80/20 view: categories sorted largest first as bars of their share of the total, a line through the running total, and a dashed line at the threshold.

What drives or moves a total Ranking, top to bottom Share of one whole

Best for

  • The few causes behind most of a total: ticket causes, defects, returns, costs
  • Deciding where to act first

Least useful for

  • Time order (use bar)
  • Fewer than four categories
  • Negative values

The table it needs

One row is: One row per category, each named once. How it is built: Rows sorted largest first as bars of their share of the total, a line through the running total and a dashed line at the threshold (80% by default). Reads well with 4 to 25 rows.

OptionHoldsRequiredWhat it does
labelcategoryyesField naming each category.
valuenumberyesField with each category's count or amount. Zero and negative values are left out.

rings

Concentric progress rings, one per row from the outside in, each filled to its share of target; past the target a second lap shows how far over.

Actual against target or plan A headline number Comparing amounts across categories

Best for

  • Progress on one to four goals in a compact tile: activity, product targets

Least useful for

  • More than four goals (use meter)
  • Comparing sizes, as inner rings are shorter

The table it needs

One row is: One row per category, each named once. How it is built: One ring per row from the outside in, filled to value over target; past the target a second lap shows how far over. Reads well with 1 to 4 rows.

OptionHoldsRequiredWhat it does
labelcategoryyesField naming each goal.
valuenumberyesField with the amount reached.
targetnumberyesField with the goal amount.

rose

A polar area chart (a Nightingale rose) for a cycle that wraps round, such as hours of the day or months of the year: one equal wedge per row, clockwise from twelve o'clock, its area true to its value.

Patterns across two dimensions or a cycle Comparing amounts across categories

Best for

  • Cycles that wrap round: hours of the day, months of the year, directions

Least useful for

  • Categories with no cycle (use bar)
  • Precise comparisons

The table it needs

One row is: One row per category, each named once. How it is built: One equal wedge per row, clockwise from twelve o'clock, its area true to value; several y fields stack. Reads well with 4 to 36 rows.

OptionHoldsRequiredWhat it does
labelcategoryyesField naming each wedge, in cycle order, such as the hour or the month.
ynumber (one or more)yesField or fields with the values; each field is one ring of the stack. Up to 4 stay readable.

sankey

Flows between stages as ribbons as thick as their volume, for example traffic source to landing page to outcome.

Flows between stages or groups Nested breakdowns What drives or moves a total

Best for

  • Flows through stages: traffic source to page to outcome, budget to spend
  • Where volume goes and where it is lost

Least useful for

  • Flows that loop back between the same groups (use chord)
  • Many tiny flows

The table it needs

One row is: One row per flow, from a source to a target. How it is built: Each row is a ribbon from source to target, as thick as value; nodes stack into stages left to right. Reads well with 2 to 80 rows.

OptionHoldsRequiredWhat it does
sourcecategoryyesField naming where each flow starts.
targetcategoryyesField naming where each flow ends.
valuenumberyesField with each flow's volume.

scatter

One dot per row placed by two numbers, to show how they relate.

How two measures relate How values spread Exact values and lookup

Best for

  • Whether two measures move together: growth and margin, price and volume
  • Segments and quadrants, and the accounts that stand out

Least useful for

  • One measure only (use histogram)
  • Trends over time (use line)

The table it needs

One row is: One row per thing measured (a deal, a ticket, a response); the chart counts or spreads them. How it is built: One dot per row at x and y (both numbers); size and series add a third and fourth field, and label names each dot. Reads well with 6 to 2000 rows.

OptionHoldsRequiredWhat it does
xnumberyesNumeric field along the horizontal axis.
ynumberyesNumeric field along the vertical axis.
sizenumberField sizing each dot by area, making a bubble chart: four times the value, twice the radius. Bigger bubbles are drawn first.
seriescategoryField that groups the dots by color. Up to 3 groups stay distinct.
labelcategoryField naming each dot in its tooltip.

slope

Each item's move between two points in time, as a line from a left column to a right one on one shared scale.

Change between two points Ranking, top to bottom

Best for

  • Two points in time: H1 against H2, last year against this
  • Seeing who rose, who fell and who swapped places

Least useful for

  • More than two periods (use line or bump)
  • More than about 15 items, where lines tangle (use dumbbell)

The table it needs

One row is: One row per category, each named once. How it is built: One line per row from its from value on the left to its to value on the right, on one shared scale. Reads well with 2 to 15 rows.

OptionHoldsRequiredWhat it does
labelcategoryyesField naming each row.
fromnumberyesField with the earlier value (left column).
tonumberyesField with the later value (right column).

sunburst

A hierarchy as rings: the inner ring splits the total by the first level, each outer ring splits its parent's slice by the next level, in lighter tints of the parent's color.

Nested breakdowns Share of one whole

Best for

  • Two or three level part-to-whole: revenue by product, then region
  • An overview that invites a closer look

Least useful for

  • Precise comparisons (use icicle or hbar)
  • Deep levels with long names (use icicle)

The table it needs

One row is: One row per leaf of the hierarchy, its levels in columns from the top down. How it is built: The inner ring splits the total by the first level; each outer ring splits its parent by the next level, by the sum of value. Reads well with 4 to 120 rows.

OptionHoldsRequiredWhat it does
levelscategory (one or more)yesFields from the top level down, one ring each, for example ["product", "region"]. Up to 3.
valuenumberyesField sizing the slices. Zero and negative values are left out.

table

Rows and columns.

Exact values and lookup Comparing amounts across categories

Best for

  • Exact values, many columns, audit and export
  • Data people will look up rather than scan

Least useful for

  • Seeing a pattern at a glance (use any chart)

The table it needs

One row is: Any rows. How it is built: One line per row and one column per field (or the columns listed), formatted, sortable, with optional totals. Reads well with 1 to any number of rows.

OptionHoldsRequiredWhat it does
columnsany (one or more)Fields to show, in order. Defaults to every field in the rows.

timeline

A Gantt-style timeline: one row per task with a bar from its start to its end date, a diamond for milestones (no end), month ticks along the top and an optional today line.

Schedules and plans

Best for

  • Project plans, launch phases and milestones
  • What is late or running now

Least useful for

  • Quantities (use bar)

The table it needs

One row is: One row per category, each named once. How it is built: One row per task with a bar from start to end, a diamond where there is no end (a milestone), grouped and with a today line. Reads well with 1 to 40 rows.

OptionHoldsRequiredWhat it does
labelcategoryyesField naming each task.
startdateyesField with each task's start date, as YYYY-MM-DD or a timestamp.
enddateField with each task's end date. A row without one is drawn as a milestone.
groupcategoryField that colors tasks by team or phase, up to 8 groups.
progressnumberField with each task's share done, from 0 to 1 (values above 1 are read as percentages). Fills the bar that far and labels it after the bar.

treemap

Part-to-whole for many categories: tiles sized by value, kept close to square.

Share of one whole Nested breakdowns Comparing amounts across categories

Best for

  • Many parts of one whole: revenue by customer, spend by vendor
  • Portfolios grouped by segment

Least useful for

  • Two or three parts (use donut)
  • Precise comparisons (use hbar)
  • Negative values

The table it needs

One row is: One row per category, each named once. How it is built: One tile per row, its area its share of the sum of value, kept close to square; an optional group field clusters tiles. Reads well with 4 to 120 rows.

OptionHoldsRequiredWhat it does
labelcategoryyesField naming each tile.
valuenumberyesField sizing each tile. Zero and negative values are left out.
groupcategoryField that colors related tiles alike, up to 8 groups. Without it every tile shares one color.

variance

Variance against plan, as in financial reporting: per row a bar from a zero line to actual minus plan, right when over and left when under, colored good or bad and labelled with its sign.

Actual against target or plan What drives or moves a total Comparing amounts across categories

Best for

  • Budget against actual per line item
  • Financial variance reports where the sign and size of each miss matter

Least useful for

  • Data with no plan or budget (use hbar)

The table it needs

One row is: One row per category, each named once. How it is built: One bar per row from a zero line to value minus target, right when over and left when under, colored good or bad. Reads well with 2 to 20 rows.

OptionHoldsRequiredWhat it does
labelcategoryyesField naming each row, such as a department.
valuenumberyesField with the actual amount.
targetnumberyesField with the plan, budget or target.

waffle

Part to whole as a 10 by 10 grid where each square is one percent, filled category by category in reading order, with a legend of values and shares.

Share of one whole A headline number

Best for

  • One share people grasp at once: 37% of revenue is online
  • Two to five parts for a general audience

Least useful for

  • Many parts or shares under 1%
  • Comparing several wholes (use bar stacked to percent)

The table it needs

One row is: One row per category, each named once. How it is built: A 10 by 10 grid, one square per percent, filled category by category in row order. Reads well with 1 to 5 rows.

OptionHoldsRequiredWhat it does
labelcategoryyesField naming each category.
valuenumberyesField with each category's amount. Zero and negative values are left out.

waterfall

A bridge: how a total moves to another through increases and decreases, each floating from the running total, with totals standing on zero.

What drives or moves a total Change between two points

Best for

  • Bridges: what took revenue from Q2 to Q3, a profit and loss walk
  • Explaining a move from a start to an end

Least useful for

  • Amounts that are not changes to one total (use bar)

The table it needs

One row is: One row per category, each named once. How it is built: Rows in order: totals stand on zero, and every other row is a change floating from the running total, up or down. Reads well with 3 to 15 rows.

OptionHoldsRequiredWhat it does
labelcategoryyesField naming each step.
valuenumberyesField with each step's change, or the amount for total rows.
